stem: According to the source, why is the height centile a critical factor when interpreting a child's blood pressure reading?

options.text: The $95^{th}$ percentile for blood pressure varies significantly based on height.
Height is used to calculate the necessary intravenous fluid volume.
Taller children are more likely to have primary essential hypertension.
It determines whether a manual or automated cuff should be used.

explanation: A child on the $5^{th}$ height centile has a lower threshold for hypertension than a child on the $95^{th}$ height centile.
rationale: Recall how the blood pressure thresholds shift when looking at the $5^{th}$ vs. $95^{th}$ centile for stature.

optionExplanations.A: A child on the $5^{th}$ height centile has a lower threshold for hypertension than a child on the $95^{th}$ height centile.
optionExplanations.B: While height influences fluid calculations, its primary role in this context is determining the normal range on blood pressure charts.
optionExplanations.C: The height centile is used for diagnostic classification rather than predicting the specific etiology of the hypertension.
optionExplanations.D: The choice of measurement device is separate from the percentile-based interpretation of the resulting numbers.
